  Details:
  Two linked efforts to make the agroverse farm-media pipeline durable and flood-proof.
  
  A) ARCHITECTURE REDESIGN (farm-media-daemon): turned a single YouTube uploader into the two-worker "Media Archive Daemon" — (1) S3 raw-archive worker streaming zip uploads per-file (junk-skipping, dedupe-vs-S3 by size) to media.agroverse.shop, and (2) shared YouTube uploader. Added English caption tracks + translated descriptions with a resume-safe daily-quota backfill, GPS reverse-geocoding into video descriptions/manifest place fields (place_name/place_geo), and schema fields (captured_at, raw_url, preview). 9 merged PRs #11-#20 (PR #20 this thread: stop backfill on YouTube daily quota exhaustion instead of infinite 30s retry; skip silent/no-speech videos).
  
  B) STORAGE MIGRATION (infra, no PR): root disk was 97% full (2.9GB free) and the whole media pipeline (inbox 7.2GB + archive work dirs ~15GB + 20 upload zips 17GB ≈ 40GB) sat on it. Provisioned 250GB gp3 EBS (vol-01b643f5629987b61, nelanco, us-east-1a), mounted /media (ext4, fstab nofail), rsync-migrated all inbox/work/zip trees byte-verified, re-pointed media_archive_daemon_config.yaml (36 refs /home/ubuntu -> /media), restarted both systemd units, symlinked old paths as compat net, chowned to ubuntu. Result: root 97% -> 47% (42GB free), /media 18% (193GB free); both services active and archiving from the new disk.
  
  Verification: rsync byte-counts matched (328 mp4s + per-dir sizes exact); config sanity check all 11 inboxes + 25 roots/zips resolve; services active, archive worker doing clean S3 skip-passes with no permission errors after chown fix.
